name: AROS
rootCause: AROS gates its reward distribution behind admin-signed messages consumed by claimPrincipal(...) and claimYield(...), but the signature scheme is replayable / forgeable: the attacker supplies fixed (r,s,v) signatures to mint/withdraw large AROS principal and yield amounts to themselves. Backed by a long chain of V3 flash loans (Moolah, Balancer, Aave, Venus and ~25 Pancake/Uniswap V3 pools) for working capital, the attacker pumps the AROS/USDT pool, replays the signed claimPrincipal and claimYield calls to extract AROS, then dumps it back into USDT, draining the AROS/USDT LP for ~$295K. Root cause is missing nonce/binding validation on the claim signatures, allowing reuse of valid admin signatures to drain rewards. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0xe89fe640ec5241edfca7d8dcae77a0a4270dee15e4bbd043fc60e393aabf41e1 Analysis: TenArmor

The DeFi project AROS on BSC was exploited. The attacker interacted with the AROS/USDT PancakeSwap liquidity pool and drained approximately $295.3K USDT.

AROS was exploited on BNB Chain on 30 May 2026, resulting in losses of approximately $295,000, with the attacker draining protocol assets via flash loans, contract calls, and signature-based withdrawals. The precise vulnerable operation is unconfirmed due to the absence of a published protocol-side postmortem. The incident involved rapid asset extraction using flash loans, approvals, and signature-based functions. Most evidence suggests a price/oracle manipulation or privileged claim/withdrawal path, but the exact contract vulnerability remains unconfirmed by the protocol due to the lack of an official postmortem or technical disclosure.
